newsitem.title: FRANCE: ROWING-REDGRAVE HELPS BRITISH FOUR TO PERFECT START.
newsitem.headline: ROWING-REDGRAVE HELPS BRITISH FOUR TO PERFECT START.

text.p: The British coxless four, including Olympic champion Steve Redgrave, made a perfect start in a World Cup rowing event on Friday by winning their heat in impressive fashion.

Redgrave, who won his fourth gold last year in Atlanta with Matthew Pinsent in a coxless pair, is now competing in the coxless four since setting his sights on a fifth Olympic title at the 2000 Sydney Games.
France and Britain dominated the first day of the three-day regatta in miserable weather in the French capital.
The host nation qualified nine boats while six British boats advanced to the next rounds.
Redgrave and Pinsent, whose association dates back to 1992 and who competed as a coxless pair until this season, recorded their 65th consecutive victory.
They and partners Tim Foster and James Cracknell look set to meet the French crew in Sunday's final.
The French four were less than a second slower than the British quartet when they won their heat on Friday.
"We'll race anyone, we don't mind," said a confident Redgrave.

In the women's single sculls, Germany's Katrin Boron, Olympic gold medallist in doubles sculls, won her heat without difficulty and will go on to face Olympic champion Katya Khotoditch of Belarus and former world champion Maria Brandin of Sweden, who also won their races.
Favourite Iztok Kop of Slovenia won his heat in the men's single sculls but the fastest qualifier was Egypt's Ibrahim Ali.
Swiss brothers Markus and Michael Gier, the lightweight double sculls Olympic champions, moved smoothly through to Saturday's semifinals.
